translation.text: Destroy all oppression from the face of the earth, and let every evil deed come to an end. Let the plant of righteousness and uprightness appear and become a blessing; deeds of righteousness and uprightness will be planted forever in joy.[a]

translation.text: Now all the righteous will escape and remain alive until they beget a thousand; they will complete all the days of their youth and their rest in peace.[a]

footnotes.text: “A thousand” retains the selected ፲፻, with descendants understood from “beget”; it is not silently changed into a thousand years. The selected word ሰንበት belongs to the sabbath/rest range, checked in actual Dillmann cols369–370. “Rest” is retained rather than asserting that the printed word simply means old age. Youth terminology is checked at col900.

translation.text: Every delightful tree will be planted on it, and vineyards will be planted on it. The vine planted on it will produce wine in abundance. Every seed sown on it—one measure will produce ten thousand; and one measure of olives will produce ten press-measures of oil.[a]

footnotes.text: Actual Dillmann col721 distinguishes the specifically numbered myriad/ten-thousand use from broader thousand uses; the selected seed-yield word is retained as ten thousand. The olive term is checked at cols719–720 and the press term at col873. “Press-measures” preserves the production-capacity image; the text gives no modern capacity or conversion, and this is not a literal agricultural forecast.

translation.text: The earth will be cleansed of all corruption, all sin, all scourging, and all suffering. Never again will I send these things on it, from generation to generation and forever.[a]

footnotes.text: The source does not express the object of “send”; “these things” resumes the preceding afflictions. The negative/repetition idiom is checked at actual Dillmann col1131 and suffering at col1304. The wording does not suppress the temporal scope or turn the divine promise into a modern safety guarantee.
